## `IMediaPlaybackSession` { #imediaplaybacksession-interface }

`public interface IMediaPlaybackSession : IDisposable`

Commands run on the owning host thread. ReadSnapshot reads only a cached, coherent struct: no JNI/ObjC polling, allocations or developer callbacks. Native adapters must tag asynchronous results with the originating revision, not with whichever source happens to be current when a callback arrives. Prepare replaces the source and clears play intention. Stop/Dispose are lossless, synchronous control commands; Dispose cancels outstanding callbacks. This contract does not yet grant background playback or a video output.

**Propriétés**

| Membre | Description |
|---|---|
| `MediaHandle Handle { get; }` |  |

**Méthodes**

|---|---|
| `MediaSnapshot ReadSnapshot()` |  |

| `void SetPlayIntent(bool play, ulong sourceRevision)` |  |
| `void Stop(ulong sourceRevision)` |  |

## `IMediaPreloadCapability` { #imediapreloadcapability-interface }

`public interface IMediaPreloadCapability : INativeCapability`

Optional short-form preloading, implemented by a media backend next to `IMediaPlaybackCapability`. The host ranks a playlist around the item on screen; the backend buffers the start of nearby items (memory for the next one, disk cache for those after) and drops work for items left behind. A session that later prepares one of these sources starts from that data. Control thread only.

**Méthodes**

| Membre | Description |
|---|---|
| `void SetPreloadQueue(IReadOnlyList<NativeMediaSource> sources, int currentIndex)` | Replaces the ranked playlist; `currentIndex` is on screen. |

## `IMediaThumbnailCapability` { #imediathumbnailcapability-interface }

`public interface IMediaThumbnailCapability : INativeCapability`

Optional poster frames for video sources: the first frame, decoded off the control thread and kept in a disk cache. `completed` runs on the control thread with a local image file path, or null when unavailable. It never runs before `RequestThumbnail` returns, even on a cache hit, so callers may request thumbnails before their own state is initialised.

**Méthodes**

| Membre | Description |
|---|---|
| `void RequestThumbnail(NativeMediaSource source, int maxWidth, Action<string> completed)` |  |

## `NativeWindowMetrics` { #nativewindowmetrics-struct }

`public struct NativeWindowMetrics : IEquatable<NativeWindowMetrics>`

Cross-platform logical viewport metrics supplied by the native host. `SafeAreaBottom` is the part of the surface under a home indicator or gesture bar; bottom bars pad their content by it. `SafeAreaTop` is the part under the status bar or a notch: zero while the window starts below it (usual on Android), its height once the app draws edge-to-edge (iOS).
